title: Berge–Jackson–Zhang conjecture on circuit double covers
statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph. A **circuit double cover** (CDC) is a set of circuits such that every edge of $G$ is covered by exactly two circuits. A graph is **cyclically $5$-edge-connected** if no edge cut of size less than $5$ separates two circuits.

**Berge–Jackson–Zhang conjecture.** If $G$ is a cyclically $5$-edge-connected cubic graph and $D$ is a set of pairwise disjoint circuits of $G$, then $D$ is a subset of a CDC, unless $G$ is the Petersen graph.

The paper states that its construction yields counterexamples to this conjecture: the relevant permutation $2$-factor is not contained in any circuit double cover. Earlier finite counterexamples were also found by computer search.
source_name: Jonas Hägglund and Arthur Hoffmann-Ostenhof, “Construction of Permutation Snarks”, arXiv:1208.3230 (2012).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.3230

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2012). “Note that finitely many counterexamples to the above conjectures were found in by computer search.”
